slides.title: S.E.A.G.R: A Socially and Emotionally Aware Greeting Robot Framework with Dual-Layer Cultural and Affective Modulation
slides.tldr: CULTURALLY AND EMOTIONALLY ADAPTIVE GREETING FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: This framework introduces a dual-layer modulation system for robotic greetings based on cultural identity and affective cues, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: SEAGR is a robotic framework that adapts greeting gestures based on user culture and emotional state.
card.key_idea: A dual-layer Sense–Think–Act architecture: Layer 1 selects cultural gestures via badge ID; Layer 2 modulates gesture amplitude and duration based on detected facial emotions.
card.evaluation: Implemented as a low-cost proof-of-concept prototype using Arduino, OpenCV, and ultrasonic sensors. No empirical user studies were conducted.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation through user studies and relies on badge-based identification, which does not generalize to all public spaces.

slides.title: Faraday Future Launches FF Nexus Academy Summer Camps for Los Angeles Students
slides.highlight: Faraday Future is implementing an embodied AI robotics education strategy through summer camps, which aligns with RwB's focus on embodied learning.

slides.title: China Unveils Humanoid AI Companion Robots to Ease Loneliness
slides.highlight: The introduction of humanoid AI companion robots to address loneliness aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Towards Agentic Agent-based Models: Feasibility, Performance, and Statistical Model Checking
slides.tldr: INTEGRATING LLM-BASED AGENTS INTO ABM SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores replacing symbolic rules in agent-based models with LLM-driven decisions, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Investigates the feasibility and impact of replacing symbolic ABM decision rules with LLM-based tool calls.
card.key_idea: Extends a Mesa Schelling segregation model where one agent uses a local LLM (Qwen3.5) via tool calls to classify neighbors' similarity.
card.evaluation: Compared original vs. LLM-extended models using MultiVeStA statistical model checking; tested four Qwen3.5 model sizes (0.8b to 9b) on semantic tasks.
card.limitation: Small LLMs exhibit semantic and operational failures; larger models are reliable but introduce significant runtime overhead.

slides.title: Social Simulations: from Agent-Based Modeling to Digital Twins
slides.highlight: This work traces the shift from classical agent-based models to LLM-enhanced simulations and Social Digital Twins, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: A survey of social simulations evolving from classical agent-based modeling to LLM-enhanced agents and social digital twins.
card.key_idea: Progresses from rule-based ABMs to LLM-driven agents for linguistic interaction, culminating in data-driven Social Digital Twins that mirror specific real-world socio-technical systems.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via literature survey and references to studies on opinion dynamics, persuasion, and polarization using LLM agents and network structures.
card.limitation: High sensitivity to prompt design, potential for model biases, and significant computational costs for high-fidelity digital twins.

slides.title: On the Structure of Address in Multi-Party Dialogue: From Discrete Labels to Continuous Levels
slides.tldr: CONTINUOUS ADDRESSEE DETECTION IN MULTI-PARTY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This work explores addressee detection as a continuous phenomenon rather than discrete labels, analyzing its relationship with gaze and backchannels. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Address in multi-party dialogue is better modeled as a continuous level than as discrete labels.
card.key_idea: A latent-variable model transforms categorical annotator judgments into continuous address levels, representing addressivity as a graded property rather than a multi-class classification task.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Japanese triadic dialogue corpus using Bayesian mixed-effects models; continuous levels showed better predictive fit (ELPD) for turn-taking, gaze, and backchannels.
card.limitation: Limited to Japanese triadic discussions; address levels were inferred from only three categorical annotations per turn.

slides.title: How Reliable Are Multimodal Signals of Conversational State? Evidence from Remote Dyadic Collaborative Tasks
slides.tldr: EVALUATING MULTIMODAL SIGNALS FOR CONVERSATIONAL STATE
slides.highlight: This work evaluates the reliability of interactional, acoustic, and linguistic features for predicting cognitive load and power roles, supporting HyECHO's focus on robust multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Multimodal signals for conversational state are often unreliable, reflecting speaker identity or task-specific vocabulary instead.
card.key_idea: A three-dimensional framework (prediction, generalizability, reliability) evaluating interactional, acoustic, and linguistic features using LODO, LOCO, and speaker-normalized ICC on the AVCAffe dataset.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 53 dyads across 9 tasks using Random Forest, CCC for cognitive load, and macro F1 for power.
card.limitation: Conversational power prediction remained near chance; results are limited to Zoom-mediated dyadic interactions.

slides.title: PACE: Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC PERSONA ADAPTATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for humanoid robots to dynamically synthesize tailored, psychologically grounded personas through user interaction, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PACE enables humanoid robots to dynamically generate tailored personas through interactive Q&A to improve HRI quality.
card.key_idea: An interactive elicitation pipeline extracts psychological dimensions (traits, values, motivations) to compile structured persona prompts, which are then mapped to Ameca's multimodal facial and vocal behaviors.
card.evaluation: Tested with 25 participants using BFI-44, GSS, and economic games. PACE significantly outperformed a static baseline in psychometric alignment, trust, and persona consistency.
card.limitation: Relies on cloud-based LLM inference and ASR, causing potential latency and transcription errors in noisy environments.

slides.title: The World According to a Social Robot -- Augmenting Human-Robot Dialogue With Vision Language Models
slides.highlight: This research explores using Vision Language Models with a Pepper robot to enhance human-robot interaction by incorporating visual context into dialogue. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Integrating Vision Language Models into a Pepper robot enables more natural, context-aware human-robot dialogues.
card.key_idea: A Pepper robot uses Pixtral-12B to process periodic camera images and user utterances, incorporating visual context into responses via zero-shot prompting.
card.evaluation: Tested across five real-world scenarios; compared response times between Mistral and GPT-4o mini. Results show moderate latency increases (approx. 400ms for Mistral).
card.limitation: The robot's fixed gaze limits environmental perception, and the model occasionally over-describes scenes instead of focusing on specific details.

slides.title: Modeling turn-taking with distant viewing: investigating silence thresholds in human and AI-generated discourse
slides.tldr: ANALYSIS OF SILENCE GAPS IN HUMAN AND AI DISCOURSE
slides.highlight: This study examines silence thresholds and turn-taking in human and AI-generated audiovisual material, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Study compares silence gaps in human sitcoms versus AI-generated synthetic podcasts.
card.key_idea: Analysis of turn-taking silence thresholds across speaker gender and production settings using fundamental-frequency estimation in Praat.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 30 US sitcoms and 51 Google NotebookLM synthetic podcasts; results based on silence gap measurements.

slides.title: SpEmoC: A Balanced Speaker-Segment Multimodal Emotion Benchmark
slides.highlight: This work introduces SpEmoC, a balanced multimodal dataset for emotion recognition in conversations, which supports HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: SpEmoC is a balanced, large-scale multimodal emotion benchmark featuring 30k synchronized video, audio, and text clips.
card.key_idea: A hybrid pipeline using pretrained models and human validation to curate class-balanced speaking segments from movies, employing movie-level splits to ensure robust model generalization.
card.evaluation: Benchmarked five SOTA models (e.g., EMOE, TCL-MAP) on SpEmoC, MELD, and CAER using Weighted F1 and Macro-F1; results show significantly reduced class imbalance gaps.
card.limitation: Demographic attributes are approximate, inferred from visual content and potentially affected by makeup, lighting, or role-based appearance.

slides.title: Imitation of Arm Gestures by the Semi-Humanoid Robot NICO
slides.tldr: HUMAN ARM GESTURE IMITATION FOR SEMI-HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research develops a system for a semi-humanoid robot to imitate human arm gestures using MediaPipe pose-estimation and analytical geometry, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A system for the NICO robot to imitate human arm gestures using monocular RGB input.
card.key_idea: Combines MediaPipe pose and hand landmark extraction with analytical geometry to compute joint angles, which are then linearly mapped to NICO's specific motor configurations.
card.evaluation: Tested with six participants across 11 poses and three viewing angles. Results show moderate accuracy for most joints, with MAEs between 10° and 34°.
card.limitation: High reconstruction error for forearm rotation (50.1° MAE) and sensitivity to self-occlusions in complex poses.

slides.title: Mixed-Agent Museum Tour Guide Design Improves Gendered Learning Outcomes and Visitor Preferences
slides.highlight: This research explores a mixed-agent system combining a physical robot and a virtual agent to enhance engagement and learning, relating to HyECHO's focus on hybrid human-AI team states and engagement.

card.one_liner: A mixed-agent robot tour guide improves learning performance for women and increases overall visitor preference.
card.key_idea: A physical robot (Toyota HSR) paired with a gimbal-projected virtual agent using diverse conversational styles (storytelling and bantering) to simulate a dyadic human-like tour experience.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study (N=30) using pre/post-quizzes, UES/QoE surveys, behavioral sensors (ArUco markers), and interviews. Results show significant learning gains for female participants.
card.limitation: Conducted in a controlled lab setting with a slow robot walking speed (0.8 km/h) and reliance on ArUco markers.

slides.title: Dialogue Summarization with Emotion Dynamics Using Topic- and Participant-Centric Decomposition
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL DIALOGUE SUMMARIZATION WITH EMOTION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to model semantic and emotion dynamics in multimodal dialogues via topic- and participant-centric decomposition, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: A multi-agent framework for dialogue summarization that preserves both semantic content and emotional trajectories.
card.key_idea: Adapts Chain-of-Agents to decompose dialogues into topic-centric and participant-centric views, integrating multimodal emotion recognition to generate summaries reflecting emotional flow.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on AMI and IEMOCAP datasets using BLANC-help for content and novel trajectory metrics (Levenshtein, n-grams, Jaccard, Cosine) for emotion preservation.
card.limitation: Requires high-quality individual audio/video streams and may suffer from information loss during intermediate aggregation stages.
